- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.75) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days); apply a 2–5 day decay filter to smooth out overreaction.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; check for 3–5 day lag in sentiment-to-forecast alignment.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence; if below, increase by 1–2% per day.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often underestimates near-term (first 7–10 days) if sentiment is volatile; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to early days if sentiment is mixed or rising.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., 0.75 → 0.25 → 0.75), model tends to mispredict direction; use sentiment momentum (last 3 days) as a proxy for directionality.
